title: Compact coverage scratchpad & run-rate estimate
content:
Purpose: quick cross-functional tally of owners, outstanding asks and estimated effort to cover an impending weekend surge window. Use this as a short-lived run-rate estimate (hours/day) to decide whether to call for temporary standby coverage.

Last updated: 2026-11-10 (Aisha)
Context notes: sprint freeze next Tue -> limited rotations; this sheet surfaces single-point dependencies and rough effort to keep endpoints at SLO for 72-hour window. Not a replacement for oncall rota but an operational prompt for product/ops decisions.

TABLE (columns: Owner | Team/Area | Ask / Deliverable | Estimated hrs (72h window) | Criticality (P1/P2/P3) | Blockers / Notes | Follow-up owner):
Aisha Kapoor | product-ops | finalize fallback routing policy + checklist | 6 | P1 | needs SRE review of throttles (JIRA-OPS-1189) | Mei Chen
Mei Chen | eng-sre | standby runbook + quick smoke test for EU region | 10 | P1 | limited SRE headcount Fri-Sun | Tomás Rivera
Tomás Rivera | platform-engineering | reserve burst pool (2x small GPU) + confirm autoscale policy | 8 | P1 | cloud quota ticket open (CONF-5213) | Tomás Rivera
Jordan Lee | hosting-api | short-term rate limit bump plan + client comms draft | 3 | P2 | product approval needed | Aisha Kapoor
Priya Nair | customer-success | prepare support canned replies + escalation tree | 4 | P2 | legal signoff for troubleshooting template | Legal: Zoe Park
Zoe Park | legal & compliance | quick review of support template (privacy checklist) | 2 | P3 | low-risk, confirm data exposure lines | Zoe Park
Ethan Brooks | observability | add ephemeral dashboard (latency + 5xx) + alert thresholds | 5 | P1 | needs access to prod telemetry view | Ethan Brooks
Sofia Martinez | solutions-eng | patch guidance for top-3 enterprise customers | 3 | P2 | depends on Jordan for comms | Sofia Martinez
Lina Gomez | billing | estimate potential usage spike cost delta (USD) | 2 | P3 | quick cost model attached below | Lina Gomez
Marcus Holt | product-hosted-api | quick A/B rollback plan + flagging list | 4 | P1 | coordinate with platform-engineering for immediate flips | Marcus Holt

Aggregate quick sums: total estimated effort (hrs) across listed owners = 47 hrs over 72h window. Run-rate = 47 hrs / 3 days = ~15.7 hrs/day.
Assumptions and caveats: estimates are rough; they assume owners split work evenly during their normal shift windows. Does not include full oncall duration (24x7) — this is incremental effort to maintain SLOs in face of surge.

Cost sketch (from Lina): estimated extra infra cost = ~$1,200/day if burst pool used (2 small GPUs + bandwidth). Support and SRE overtime not included (ballpark add +$2.5k/day if >3 engineers escalated).

Risk banding (quick):
- If we staff owners at run-rate (~16 hrs/day) -> expectation: maintain SLO, avoid major rollbacks; residual risk: medium (P2 events possible).
- If we staff only 8 hrs/day -> expectation: reactive posture, potential user-facing latency spikes; residual risk: high (P1 incidents).

Recommended immediate next steps (short actionable):
1) Confirm burst pool reservation (Tomás) by EOD 2026-11-10.
2) SRE to publish standby runbook + smoke test checklist (Mei) by 2026-11-11 morning.
3) Product to approve client comms draft and rollback flag list (Jordan + Marcus) by 2026-11-11 noon.
4) Billing to run a 24-hour cost drill with actual metrics (Lina) and share result in #ops-costs.

Notes / open questions:
- Who owns after-hours escalation if multiple P1s trigger? Proposed: rotate between Mei and Tomás, escalate to Marcus if product-level decision needed.
- Should we proactively inform top-5 enterprise customers? Solutions-eng recommends yes but wants product signoff.

Change log:
2026-11-03 created by Aisha (initial scratchpad)
2026-11-05 updated: added cost sketch (Lina)
2026-11-10 updated: final owner confirmations and run-rate calc (Aisha)
notes: This sheet is intentionally compact — use it as a transient operational artifact. Move persistent items to the ops runbook if we decide to keep coverage pattern recurring.
